rename.from: Abnormal Memory Consumption After Upgrading to AWS Go SDK v2 While Mounting Ceph S3

body:
> "HeapReleased": 6269190144, // 5.84 GB

This looks like Go has freed the memory but it hasn't been returned to the OS.

This can happen if the memory gets fragmented.

Things to try

`export GOGC=20` that will make the garbage collector work harder at the cost of more CPU.

`--use-mmap` causes rclone to allocate buffers directly from the os which it can completely free. 

`export GODEBUG=madvdontneed=1` this tells go to release memory to the OS more aggressively 

I'm not at my computer now so can't look at your trace but hopefully that will give you something to try

> GODEBUG=madvdontneed=1

Just FYI, the change requiring this was reverted in 1.16: https://github.com/golang/go/issues/42330

---

The only other relevant & relatively recent memory change in Golang is the THP handling: https://go.dev/doc/gc-guide#Linux_transparent_huge_pages

You can try adding `GODEBUG=disablethp=1` to the runtime environment to revert that change and see if that improves things.

There was also this issue with 1.24: https://github.com/golang/go/issues/72991

The fix for that was back-ported to the 1.24 release branch, but it missed the cutoff for 1.24.5: https://github.com/golang/go/commit/390ffce7d60abf7d5317c0a78beef64affd0059a

You can try building rclone with 1.23 (because it doesn't have the above issue) and see if that solves the issue.

> You can try building rclone with 1.23 (because it doesn't have the above issue) and see if that solves the issue.

It doesn't seem to improve. Memory is nearing OOM after writing around 300K files. Now proceeding with deletion to see if RSS can decrease.

Is there a way to roll back to AWS SDK v1 to verify if this issue was introduced by the SDK upgrade?

Great, that solves one of your issues. I will leave it to @ncw for the v2 SDK usage, because I am not very familiar with those parts of the codebase.

FWIW, I did find this, but it seems to be closed with no proper resolution: https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/issues/2706

Seems to be the only middleware in the stack that actually does a deep clone of the request.

issue.title: backend/s3: Fix memory leak by cloning strings #8683

repository.name: rclone
repository.description: "rsync for cloud storage" - Google Drive, S3, Dropbox, Backblaze B2, One Drive, Swift, Hubic, Wasabi, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob, Azure Files, Yandex Files

#### What is the purpose of this change?
To addresses a potential memory leak in the S3 backend where 
strings extracted from large API responses were keeping the entire 
response in memory. The issue occurs because Go strings share underlying 
memory with their source, preventing garbage collection of large XML 
responses even when only small substrings are needed.
